q: The linear-fit slope a(t) of K_min against x = log(1/eps)/loglog(1/eps) increased from 1.67 at t=1 to 3.24 at t=10 in our replication. Is this a genuine slow t-dependence of the pre-factor, or an artifact of the accessible eps range (10^-2 to 10^-10) being bounded from below by double precision, so that the asymptotic slope is only visible at eps that we cannot resolve on a 64-bit float?
basis: We observed a monotone drift in fitted slope a(t) across t={1,2,5,10} even though the paper's bound implies a t-independent pre-factor on the log/loglog term. Extending to lower eps hits the IEEE floor at ~1e-16.
next_steps: Repeat the K_min scan in mpmath at 80- and 160-bit precision, extend the eps grid to 1e-15, 1e-20, 1e-30, and re-fit; check whether a(t) collapses to a t-independent constant at those larger x values or persists as a genuine t-drift.

q: How sensitive is the observed K_min(t,eps) curve to eigenvalue clustering near the boundary +-1 of the spectrum? Chebyshev polynomials are steepest there, so we conjecture that a Hamiltonian with a spectral gap between max|lambda| and ||H|| yields materially smaller K_min at the same t and eps.
basis: Our fixed 4x4 test Hermitian had lambda_max = 1.0000 exactly at the boundary (largest eigenvalue attains the norm). We did not sweep spectral shape.
next_steps: Regenerate H over an ensemble parameterized by spectral gap g = 1 - max|lambda|/(||H||) in {0.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5}, run the K_min scan for each, and see whether the slope a(t) and intercept b(t) shift with g.

q: The Jacobi-Anger reconstruction of exp(-iHt) requires the specific Bessel-weighted polynomial J_0(t) + 2 sum (-i)^k J_k(t) T_k. What single-QSP-shot phase sequence produces this polynomial as one U_phi(H), rather than as a linear combination of many T_k(H)? Is there a numerically stable Remez-style compiler that outputs those phases in O(K polylog K) time for practical K in the range we exercised (K up to ~30)?
basis: Our C3 check used the trivial all-zero phase sequence, which realizes only T_d, not the Bessel-weighted sum. We showed the mechanism but not the compiled-simulation-in-one-shot instance the paper builds toward.
next_steps: Implement pyqsp or QSPPACK's completion algorithm, target the Jacobi-Anger polynomial explicitly, and empirically measure (i) phase-list numerical stability, (ii) compiled unitary error vs the direct expm ground truth, as a function of K.

q: Our block-encoding W(H) required dense computation of sqrt(I - H^2), which is O(n^3) classically. In the sparse-oracle model the paper actually assumes, what is the number of oracle queries per Chebyshev step, and where does the crossover point sit versus higher-order Trotter-Suzuki for representative condensed-matter Hamiltonians (Heisenberg chain, Fermi-Hubbard) at instance sizes reachable on a modern CPU (say n = 8 to 16 qubits)?
basis: The classical dense simulation used here masks the query-model structure the paper's headline complexity depends on; sparse-access is what the O(td||H||_max + ...) query bound is denominated in.
next_steps: Implement a sparse-oracle mock (row/column oracles for a Heisenberg-XXZ chain up to 12 sites), instrument oracle-call counts inside a QSP-based simulator, and compare total call count vs a 4th-order Trotter-Suzuki simulator on the same H at matched final-state fidelity.

q: The QSP phase-sequence compilation step (the Haah / Chao-Ding-Vuillot / Ying / Dong-Meng-Whaley optimization) is the practical bottleneck at large degree; textbook implementations lose numerical precision at d > 100 or so. In an end-to-end fairness study (compile + simulate + measure), how does the total numerical error stack up against Trotter-Suzuki of matched circuit depth on the same 4-qubit H used here, and at what (t, eps) does QSP become the better numerical choice, not just the better asymptotic choice?
basis: We deliberately bypassed the compiler by using the T_d-realizing zero-phase sequence, so our C3 test says nothing about the compilation-error budget that dominates real QSP implementations.
next_steps: Use pyqsp to compile phases for the Jacobi-Anger polynomial at d in {10, 20, 40, 80}, simulate the full block-unitary, and produce a (t, eps) map showing where compiled-QSP error < compiled-Trotter-Suzuki error at matched query count.
